findings.title: Committed client claims still accept the wrong operation and status
findings.observation: For a COMMITTED claim, the verifier derives only an aggregate resource from the path and checks that claim.requestId occurs somewhere in that aggregate's public audit IDs. It never compares method, exact path or status with the authoritative event or a parsed transcript request. CODEX produces no parsed transcript requests, transcript binding is substring presence, and objective results remain labels.
findings.trigger: Use a real request ID from a synthetic Idea or project, then describe a different endpoint or response status on the same aggregate; keep the required IDs and objective labels in a structurally valid transcript.
findings.impact: The verifier returns PASS for client actions and objective claims that did not occur. A hand-written proof can therefore transform one real audit event into another claimed workflow step, defeating AC-15's no-static-substitution requirement.

evidence.description: At the exact head, a real authoritative IDEA_CREATED request ID was claimed as POST /api/v1/ideas/{sameIdeaId}/promotions with status 299 and outcome COMMITTED. The verifier returned accepted=true and reported the underlying authoritative event as IDEA_CREATED.
evidence.reference: reviewer same-resource wrong-operation/status counterexample at dc562757d98ab74adc54833c46286112c58d34de

evidence.description: The COMMITTED branch checks only authoritativeRequestIds.get(resourceId).has(requestId) and immediately continues; claim.method, exact claim.path and claim.status are unused.
The transcript binding checks only whether run/resource/request ID strings occur in transcriptText, so it does not establish the committed operation or objective result.
The new wrong-path negative changes an Idea claim into an unrelated Project path without a projectId; it tests resource classification, not a different operation/status on the same resource.
The exact committed Codex and Claude records both pass against their real ignored transcripts and the live proof API, confirming the positive path while leaving the discriminator bypass.
AC-15 and the approved plan require actual client execution and prohibit static substitution without live request/resource correlation.

findings.remediation: For every COMMITTED claim, bind method, exact path and status to a parsed client request/response event or to authoritative public audit fields with an explicit event-to-operation mapping; retain the aggregate request-ID check. Parse the committed Codex operations as well as Claude operations, and derive each objective result from explicit matched evidence instead of accepting labels. Add same-resource wrong-endpoint, wrong-status and unsupported-objective negatives.
findings.verification: Both current real client records still pass; an IDEA_CREATED request ID cannot be presented as promotion/status 299; any same-resource wrong endpoint or status fails; and removing the transcript operation needed by an objective makes that objective fail.

findings.title: Child-resource writes are committed without matching public reads
findings.observation: The current implementation maps every scenario result ref to a direct or paginated public read and requires an exact ID match.
findings.trigger: A normal, recovered or terminal-replayed journal entry contains a child resource reference.
findings.impact: The exact child must be publicly present before COMMITTED/PASS; missing or mismatched children now fail closed.

evidence.description: Exact report/progress reads pass, mismatched progress fails, and terminal replay performs zero writes while reading reports and progress.

findings.verification: Targeted unit tests and exact-head CI verify normal, recovery and terminal readback behavior.

findings.title: IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS is persisted as terminal rejection
findings.observation: The current recovery helper recognizes the bounded retry contract, preserves exact bytes/key and leaves exhaustion OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
findings.trigger: Recovery receives one or more 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS responses.
findings.impact: Temporary concurrency no longer becomes terminal local rejection and the original intent remains resumable.

evidence.description: The exact-head regression proves retry-success after two sends and OUTCOME_UNKNOWN after three bounded in-progress responses, with identical body and key.

findings.verification: Targeted unit tests and exact-head CI pass.

required_actions.action: Bind every COMMITTED claim's method, exact path and status—and each objective result—to parsed execution or authoritative event evidence, with discriminating same-resource negative tests.
Publicly reconcile each exact child resource before COMMITTED/PASS and on terminal replay.
Implement and test bounded IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS recovery with frozen bytes and key.
